author: cmungall
body: CHAC1 and CHAC2 have confusing seemingly conflicting stories when Reactome annotations are combined from elsewhere: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q9BUX1/entry MF: BP: The MF one is incorrect and comes from an incorrect Reactome mapping: https://reactome.org/content/detail/R-HSA-6785928 It should be mapped to - Glutathione-specific gamma-glutamylcyclotransferases (consistent with the FlyBase-provided annotation) Not to - gamma-glutamylcyclotransferases Two asides here: - shouldn't we be catching these as part of the global RHEA-EC-GO-Reactome reconciliation? cc @balhoff - The names make it seem like these two MFs should be related via is-a, but in fact I think the current sibling relationship is correct. EC terminology is odd... ACTIONS: -[ ] Fix the Reactome MF mapping The above is a straighforward incorrect mapping. the next is more nuanced. CHAC1/2 is involved *after* synthesis of GSH, when GSC is recycled. According to GO BP start/end rules, anything happening after synthesis should *not* be annotated to synthesis. The current GO Central annotation (catabolism) is correct. the conflicting Reactome-derived annotation is IMO incorrect. Where does it come from? If we walk up the Reactome tree: We get to Glutathione synthesis and recycling https://reactome.org/content/detail/R-HSA-174403 And this is mapped to the GO BP: I think as a *loose* mapping this is fine. The processes are clearly related. But it's not a propagatable (exact or narrow-to-broad) mapping, and treating it as such gives confusing annotations. But in MetaCyc terms, synthesis+recycling would be a superpathway of syn+catab, but we don't have such a term in GO (in general we don't have superpathway/composite/mereological sum terms). ACTIONS: - [ ] Fix the Reactome BP mapping. Options: - map to a broader GO term (GSH metabolism is better but it's not actually the correct semantics, since this is a superclass not superpwathway) - remove the mapping - map the individual steps to BPs (I think this is best) - use a non-exact mapping predicate (would likely require changes in the Reactome database) @deustp01, I assigned you since I believe these need to be activated at the Reactome end, but lmk if I should assign someone else. This touches on a lot of things that have been discussed on the ontology calls lately with @pgaudet @sjm41, but I put in the annotation tracker.
title: Incorrect annotations to CHAC1 and CHAC2 from Reactome annotation

author: deustp01
body: > Fix the Reactome BP mapping. Options: > map to a broader GO term (GSH metabolism is better but it's not actually the correct semantics, since this is a superclass not superpwathway) > remove the mapping > map the individual steps to BPs (I think this is best) > use a non-exact mapping predicate (would likely require changes in the Reactome database) I am going to use the broader term for now, despite the arguments, because as far as I can see this is how we handle the interconnected processes of nucleotide synthesis, salvage (which is equivalent to "recycling" here), and catabolism. See screenshot from https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/term/GO:0043173. And indeed the overall Reactome pathway consists of catabolic, and synthetic steps, which are interconnected much like their nucleotide counterparts. It is feasible to attach distinct BP terms to individual reaction steps, but Reactome allows only one BP term per event instance and, looking at the overall cyclic process, I can't make a single reaction part_of two processes as is needed. Meanwhile, here's what looks like a very similar discussion of NAD(P) process boundaries to throw into the mix [NAD(P) metabolic process terms #29050](https://github.com/geneontology/go-ontology/issues/29050) I may well be missing something here - let me know.

author: deustp01

True. The Reactome mapping is too broad, now fixed as suggested; also added a literature reference (PMID: 27913623) with evidence for the narrower mapping.

author: deustp01
body:
And finally, 

> shouldn't we be catching these as part of the global RHEA-EC-GO-Reactome reconciliation? cc @balhoff

Eventually, yes. @ukemi , @sjm41, and I are systematically working through Reactome metabolism as part of a grand project to build integrated representations of human, mouse and fly metabolism, and as we go are finding and fixing wrong chemicals to conform to RHEA and suboptimal GO BP and MF terms. "Biological oxidations" is on the to-do list for this project. (My previous guess that we had handled glutathione as part of amino acid metabolism, which is higher on the to-do list, was wrong.)
